open_points.subject: A21
open_points.text:
state2_security_gate_pass
<-> every_required_category_has_one_outcome
    AND every_APPLICABLE_references_an_accepted_decision
    AND no_UNRESOLVED

2. Every reference resolves to an indexed item, and every APPLICABLE category
   references at least one indexed accepted decision of States 0–2.
open_points.question: Does one unresolved reference make state2_security_gate_pass false when its APPLICABLE category also references a valid accepted decision, and if so which formal-invariant conjunct expresses that requirement?
options: Any unresolved reference fails the gate, so the formal invariant needs an explicit all-references-resolve conjunct.
The formal invariant is exhaustive and the unresolved additional reference does not fail the gate; the Required tests item must be weakened.
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit every_reference_resolves_to_an_indexed_item conjunct to the formal invariant.

witness.initial: All required categories have one outcome, there is no UNRESOLVED outcome, and one APPLICABLE category references accepted decision A16 plus a nonexistent item X99.
events: The workbench evaluates the formal invariant.
The workbench evaluates Required tests item 2.
outcomes: The formal invariant passes because the category references an accepted decision and the other stated conjuncts hold.
Required tests item 2 fails because X99 does not resolve to an indexed item.
witness.observer: The author attempting to advance to State 3

open_points.subject: A21
open_points.text: Every reference resolves to an indexed item
open_points.question: Which index is authoritative, which item kinds it contains, how references are qualified across States 0–2, and what happens if the same unqualified identifier matches more than one indexed item?
options: Use one global, uniquely keyed index containing every indexed artifact from States 0–2.
Use only decision indexes, despite the broader word “item”.
Resolve against state-local indexes using an unstated precedence order.
open_points.default_guess: Use one global index with unique identifiers across States 0–2 and refuse missing or ambiguous matches.

witness.initial: Two State 0–2 indexes contain different items under the same unqualified identifier A16.
outcomes: A global-index implementation refuses A16 as ambiguous.
A state-precedence implementation resolves A16 to one item and may accept the review.
witness.observer: The review author and the State 3 gate

open_points.subject: A21
open_points.text: Every reference resolves to an indexed item
open_points.question: Does “Every reference” mean only entries in each category's `references:` field, or also identifiers appearing in `affected:`, rationales, consequences, and surrounding prose?
options: Only values in the structured `references:` field are references for this rule.
Every recognizable item identifier anywhere in the complete review record is checked.
Structured references and rationale citations are checked, but `affected:` entries are not.
open_points.default_guess: Treat only entries in the structured `references:` field as references; validate `affected:` under a separately stated rule if desired.

witness.initial: The review contains `browser_boundary: NOT_APPLICABLE` with K-11 only in its rationale and contains M27 and M28 only in an `affected:` list.
events: The linter checks the complete review record.
outcomes: A field-scoped implementation checks neither K-11 nor M27/M28 under this sentence.
A record-wide implementation treats K-11 and M27/M28 as references and requires all of them to resolve.
witness.observer: The review author through differing lint diagnostics

open_points.subject: A21
open_points.text: at least one indexed accepted decision of States 0–2
open_points.question: What exact indexed item kinds and metadata make an item an “accepted decision” in each of States 0, 1, and 2, particularly for State 0 K-items and State 1 models that are not headed “Accepted decision”?
options: Only items explicitly typed and indexed as accepted decisions qualify.
Every closed K-item, model, or A-decision in States 0–2 qualifies as an accepted decision.
Qualification is inferred from headings or document location.
open_points.default_guess: Require an explicit indexed item type and accepted status; do not infer acceptance from prose or location.

witness.initial: An APPLICABLE category's only reference is an indexed State 0 K-item whose heading does not call it an accepted decision.
events: The linter determines whether the category has at least one indexed accepted decision.
outcomes: An implementation treating closed K-items as accepted decisions accepts the category.
An implementation requiring explicit accepted-decision metadata refuses the category.
witness.observer: The review author and the State 3 gate
